As a westerner and a skeptic I never put much stock into eastern sciences and mysticism or whatever you want to call mindful meditation. Gave it a try anyway. Had some very strange experiences. Keep in mind I have no background in this, I know almost nothing about meditation and am really new, I am just trying to describe my experiences as accurately as I can.

Some times, if i kind of get into the zone, i'll feel like a rush of energy starting from a point like the top back part of my skull, showering down my spine and through my whole body, seems fairly quickly like 10-15 seconds until the shower kind of dissipates through my body and I can't feel it anymore, then it is gone. It is a very euphoric feeling showering down the top of the skull down your spine then dissipating through the body. If anyone has experienced something similar on molly I would describe it like that type of euphoric explosion, except I was completely sober. This happened on my first try meditating and provided me with the evidence I needed to continue to explore mindful meditation.

Usually time fucken flies while I'm doing it. The first time I tried it I sat down cross legged and told myself I'd give it 20 minutes of really committing to it. After that endorphin head rush or however you want to describe it, I opened my eyes and checked my watch, like 4 hours had passed. Sometimes I'll count my exhales, sometimes I won't (still experimenting), but usually I'll get between 100-300 breaths I'll start feeling some crazy sensations, when I kind of lose the concentration, I'll look at my watch, yep 2 hours had passed. The time usually doesn't seem to match up with my breath count.

Random twitches, pains. I tried mindful meditation lying down a couple times. The involuntary body movements tend to happen regardless of my position, but this particular time I was lying down on my back arms straight down by my sides. When I started to feel myself kind of get into that "zone" (i usually start to notice this when I find I am really listening to my body and can feel nearly any part I think of, fingers, toes, heart beating inside of my chest), so anyway long story short, this particular time my right arm spasmed so hard that it must have lifted a good foot or so off of my bed involuntarily. Any way, I don't mind the random pains and twitches, it helps me focus on that particular part of the body and really feel it and get inside it and then the pain or spasms will go away as I kind of "breath" into them and afterward I usually feel I am in a deeper more in tune state.

Seeing colors while my eyes are closed. I don't know if this is related to meditation, since I remember seeing the same thing as a little kid when my parents told me to close my eyes don't move and go to sleep. Tough to describe but obviously the back drop is all black since my eyes are closed, but if you start to focus on that blackness, I can start to see like dots of light or energy, of no particular color, usually just kind of a lighter black (although sometimes I have seen greens and reds), sometimes they are like thousands of pixelated dots of light, kind of like someone had spritzed a water bottle sprayer at a hair salon, but light or energy as opposed to water. But the dots kind of fill the whole space, way too many to count or whatever. Other times the light appears more as waves. Like a bright point in the blackness starts to expand into an ever expanding ring then i loose it at the edge of my "vision", but then another wave will start as a point where the first one had, and expand into an ever expanding ring of light. Like when you drop a pebble into a still lake, it makes waves from that point outward in concentric circles, wave after wave, and that's when I kind of relate the visions as more "energy" like than light or particle like. Interestingly enough, I was doing this in pitch black darkness once, so I opened my eyes, and saw the same exact energy patterns without interruption, as If I had never opened my eyes at all. This confirms at least that I'm not just seeing strange nerve impulses or some shit on the inside of my eyelids.

Feeling waves of energy throughout my body. When I start to really sink into what feels like a deeper state, where I can really feel the inside of my body wherever I focus, sometimes out of nowhere I'll feel waves of energy or heat pulsating through my body. More like heat waves through my body than the endorphin shower I was describing earlier that sprinkled down my brain. But I very accurately feel these waves pulsing throughout my whole body. I'm not sure where the pulse starts, could be localized in different areas the different times this occurs, but It spreads like a thin wave through my whole body then disappears out the finger and toe tips until the next pulse. Frequency maybe about one wave pulse per second or so, but I haven't timed it, not even sure how I could since I'm sure it would break my concentration.

The sensation of spacial movement. It's more like a side to side vibration. Like my body is starting to vibrate along the frontal plane, like side to side. This one is really hard to describe the sensation. It's almost as if my body is behaving like a flickering candle in the wind, kind of flickering/vibrating left to right along the frontal plane of my body (or coronal plane if you prefer). This one is a more rare sensation of mine and honestly it is slightly disorienting, but in a fun way like a rollercoaster or a weird mirror room at the fair, except it hasn't lasted very long, maybe a second or two at a time when it rarely occurs. It is very powerful feeling in that it is undeniable, but it is very subtle in that it hasn't happened often and only when I feel like I'm real deep and listening very acutely to my body.

On an unrelated note, sometimes I can control my dreams (sometimes complete control, sometimes no control, but most often somewhere in the middle). And I dream every night for as long as I can remember. Also, I have experienced sleep paralysis one single time. The symptoms of sleep paralysis are pretty unmistakable if you've read anything about it (the sudden heaviness of the chest, shallow breathing, unable to move, hallucinations) and I had some interesting visions/ auditories that time as well. But like I said, probably not related.
